paragraphs.title: The Vision of the Bones and Their Revival

easy.explanation: Ezekiel saw a valley full of bones that were very dry.
easy.q: What did Ezekiel see in the valley?

easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Ezekiel to prophesy upon the dry bones.
easy.q: To whom was Ezekiel first commanded to prophesy?

easy.explanation: Breath entered them, and they lived.
easy.q: What entered the bodies after the sinews, flesh, and skin were formed?

answers: The bones immediately became an army
medium.explanation: There was a noise and a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone.
medium.q: What happened first after Ezekiel prophesied to the bones?

answers: Tough cords that connect and support parts of the body
medium.explanation: Sinews are strong connective cords that help hold the body together.

answers: Because there was no breath in them
medium.explanation: The bodies had been formed, but “there was no breath in them.”
medium.q: Why was Ezekiel commanded to prophesy to the wind after the bodies were formed?

answers: Bones, sinews and flesh, skin, breath and life
challenge.explanation: The bones joined, the bodies were formed, and then breath gave them life.
challenge.q: Which order correctly describes the revival of the bones?

challenge.explanation: The passage describes several stages before the army stood alive.
challenge.q: What does the movement from joined bones to a great army show?

challenge.explanation: The army is described as “an exceeding great army.”
challenge.q: Which phrase emphasizes the greatness of the army?

paragraphs.title: The Meaning of the Bones: The Revival of Israel

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “these bones are the whole house of Israel.”

answers: Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost
easy.explanation: Israel expressed despair, saying, “our hope is lost.”
easy.q: What did the people of Israel say about their condition?

easy.explanation: The Lord promised to bring them into the land of Israel.
easy.q: To what land would the Lord bring Israel?

answers: Open them and bring the people out
medium.explanation: The Lord said, “I will open your graves” and bring His people up.
medium.q: What did the Lord promise to do with the graves of His people?

answers: The people felt they had no future
The people found a new home
The people received a new king
medium.explanation: The statement expresses Israel’s deep hopelessness.
medium.q: What does “our hope is lost” mean in this passage?

answers: The Spirit causes Israel to leave the land
The Spirit gives life, and Israel knows the Lord
medium.explanation: The Lord puts His Spirit in them, gives them life, and they know that He is the Lord.
medium.q: How are the giving of the Spirit and knowing the Lord connected?

answers: It only describes a change in the bones’ appearance
It symbolizes the revival of the whole house of Israel
It explains how trees were made
challenge.explanation: The bones represent Israel, and their revival represents Israel’s restoration.
challenge.q: What meaning is given to the vision of the bones?

answers: Opening graves, giving life, and restoring the people to the land
Leaving the land, dividing, and being lost
Building trees, writing, and dividing kingdoms
challenge.explanation: The Lord promises to raise His people, give them His Spirit, and place them in their own land.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of promises made to Israel?

answers: “I the Lord have spoken it, and performed it”
challenge.explanation: The words “spoken it, and performed it” emphasize that the Lord would accomplish His promise.
challenge.q: Which statement emphasizes that the Lord’s promise would actually be fulfilled?

paragraphs.title: The Two Sticks and the Unification of the Kingdoms

easy.explanation: Ezekiel was commanded to take two sticks.
easy.q: What was Ezekiel commanded to take?

answers: For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions
easy.explanation: The first stick was for Judah and the Israelites associated with Judah.
easy.q: What was to be written on the first stick?

easy.explanation: He was to join the sticks one to another so that they became one.
easy.q: What was Ezekiel to do with the two sticks?

answers: Ephraim and the tribes of Israel associated with him
medium.explanation: Joseph’s stick was for Ephraim and all the house of Israel his companions.

answers: People or tribes associated with them
medium.explanation: The word refers to the Israelites joined or associated with Judah and Joseph.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “companions” mean in this context?

answers: So the people would ask what they meant
So the prophecy would be hidden
So he could exchange them for other sticks
medium.explanation: The people were expected to see the sticks and ask Ezekiel about their meaning.
medium.q: Why was Ezekiel to display the sticks before the people?

answers: The division of Israel into two kingdoms
The unification of Judah and Israel
The removal of the tribal names
challenge.explanation: The two sticks represented the divided kingdoms, and their union represented reunification.
challenge.q: What did joining the two sticks represent?

answers: Ezekiel writes on and joins the sticks, while the Lord makes them one
Ezekiel gathers the exiles, while the Lord writes on the sticks
Ezekiel builds the sanctuary, while the Lord explains the bones
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel performs the symbolic action, and the Lord explains its fulfillment.
challenge.q: What is the difference between Ezekiel’s action and the Lord’s promised action?

answers: The sticks were held before the people’s eyes
The breath came from four winds
challenge.explanation: The sticks were displayed publicly before the eyes of the people.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the message was intended for the people and not only for Ezekiel?

paragraphs.title: The Gathering of the Exiles and One People

easy.explanation: The Lord would take Israel from among the nations where they had been scattered.
easy.q: From where would the Lord gather the children of Israel?

easy.explanation: The Lord promised to bring them into their own land.
easy.q: Where would the Lord bring the children of Israel?

easy.explanation: They would no longer be divided into two kingdoms but would become one.
easy.q: How many kingdoms would the people have after being united?

answers: It would become one nation in the land
It would divide into many nations
medium.explanation: The Lord said, “I will make them one nation in the land.”
medium.q: What would happen to Israel after it was gathered into its land?

medium.explanation: The Lord would save them from their sinful dwellingplaces and cleanse them.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “cleanse them” mean?

answers: Israel would be one people, and the Lord would be their God
Unity would make Israel turn away from the Lord
Unity would end worship of the Lord
medium.explanation: The passage connects Israel’s unity with the Lord being their God.
medium.q: How are unity and Israel’s relationship with the Lord connected?

answers: From being scattered among the nations to becoming one people in the land
From one nation to two kingdoms
challenge.explanation: Israel would be gathered, restored to its land, and made one nation.
challenge.q: What complete change is described for Israel?

answers: The Lord saves Israel from sinful places and cleanses it
Israel is cleansed before it is scattered
Salvation prevents any return to the land
challenge.explanation: The Lord saves His people from their sinful dwellingplaces and cleanses them.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between salvation and cleansing in this passage?

challenge.explanation: The phrases “one nation” and “one king” together emphasize Israel’s unity.
challenge.q: Which wording emphasizes both political and national unity?

paragraphs.title: Davidic Rule, the Covenant of Peace, and the Sanctuary

easy.explanation: The passage says, “David my servant shall be king over them.”
easy.q: Who would be king over the people?

easy.explanation: The Lord promised to set His sanctuary in the midst of them forevermore.
easy.q: What would be placed in the midst of the people as a sign of the Lord’s presence?

easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will make a covenant of peace with them.”
easy.q: What kind of covenant would the Lord make with the people?

answers: Walk in the Lord’s judgments and observe His statutes
medium.explanation: They would walk in the Lord’s judgments and observe His statutes.
medium.q: What would the people do under David’s leadership?

medium.explanation: The word “everlasting” describes a covenant that continues without end.

answers: The Lord would be their God, and they would be His people
The Lord would depart from them
The people would belong to other nations
medium.explanation: The passage repeats the covenant relationship: the Lord would be their God and they would be His people.
medium.q: What would be the relationship between the Lord and the people after the sanctuary was placed among them?

answers: They describe united leadership, obedience, and stability
They describe division, captivity, and war
They describe abandoning the land and sanctuary
challenge.explanation: One king, obedience to the Lord, and a covenant of peace portray a united and stable people.
challenge.q: How are the king, the laws, and peace connected in the future described here?

answers: His sanctuary would be in the midst of Israel forevermore
The bones would remain in the valley
challenge.explanation: The Lord’s permanent sanctuary among Israel would demonstrate His sanctifying presence.
challenge.q: Why would the nations know that the Lord sanctifies Israel?

answers: They, their children, and their children’s children would dwell there for ever
The army stood upon its feet
challenge.explanation: The passage includes the people, their children, and their children’s children dwelling in the land forever.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Israel’s dwelling in the land would extend beyond one generation?
